h: Hull Tips: Patties, Phone Boxes and Maritime Tales
p: Keen to keep things simple? Book your session ahead, fill in waivers online and pack a bottle of water each. Comfy clothes are a must, and grip socks can usually be reused on your next visit. Little ones can get overwhelmed during busy weekend slots, so quieter times are worth looking at if you've got very young children.

Hull is a city with a personality all of its own. It was the UK City of Culture in 2017, which brought a real boost to its arts scene, and you'll notice the cream-coloured phone boxes that set it apart from the rest of the country. Foodies should try a Hull pattie, a local favourite made of seasoned mashed potato and sage, battered and fried, and best bought from a chippy.

There's lots of history to explore too. Wilberforce House, the birthplace of anti-slavery campaigner William Wilberforce, is now a museum, and the Streetlife Museum of Transport is a nostalgic treat with old bikes, cars and carriages. Hull Minster is a beautiful church at the heart of the Old Town, and the city's fishing and seafaring past pops up everywhere you look, from the marina to the waterfront by the Humber.
Shopping and food are easy to find around Princes Quay and the city centre, so you'll have plenty of options to refuel after all that bouncing.
